spec_fixture_line: F8 scratch file, but its basename appears in a census-like dir → still SAFE(stale) (D3)
intent: Same artifact as F7, except that a census-like directory holds a file naming the scratch basename. The binding sweep excludes census dirs, so the reference count stays 0 and the verdict stays SAFE(stale). This is the D3 regression test: an unfixed sweep measures 1 reference and flips the verdict to NOT-SAFE.
compat_note: verdict/receipt/targets mirror expect.* and target so a loader written for the F1–F6 shape (targets[] + expect[]) or the F9 shape (target + verdict + receipt) reads this case unchanged; targets are relative to the fixture repo root.

decoy.why_this_path: the binding D3 exclusion is the literal glob `!souji-shokunin/census/**`, so the decoy must sit under a directory literally named `census`; a directory named `census-like` would NOT be excluded, and placing the decoy there would make this case contradict itself.

build.materialize: bash setup.sh <fixture-repo-root>; this also runs `git init -q -b master` on the root when it is not already a repository (idempotent, offline, no commits), so the target sits inside a repo even when the case is invoked directly instead of by a harness
build.entry_point_fixture_contract: bash make-fixture.sh [--out] [OUT_DIR] materializes the case, then prints on stdout line 1 = the JSON contract {case,root,targets,expect} and a final line = `FIXTURE_READY <case> <absolute target path>`
build.copy: repo-tree/. is copied verbatim into <fixture-repo-root>, paths preserved

files.why: the target under test; names itself nowhere
keeps the scratch file unstaged under `git add -A` so the pushed receipt cannot mask the stale branch
seed file only; gives the fixture repo a first commit so git plumbing behaves like a real lane repo
the D3 decoy: a census-shaped row naming the scratch basename; must be excluded from the reference sweep

build.git: leave .scratch/stale-probe-f8.tmp untracked: never `git add -f` it and never commit it. The decoy may be tracked or untracked without changing the expectation, because the exclusion is by path, not by tracking state.

scratch_class: the binding spec lists `.scratch/`, `*.out`, `*.log`, checkpoint json/png and `*-draft.*` as scratch types; `.tmp` alone is not one, so the scratch class is carried by the `.scratch/` path component and the filename stays `stale-probe-*.tmp`
notes: Materialize only repo-tree/. Never copy this case directory (or expected.json/setup.sh) into the swept fixture repo: those files name the target basename by design and would count as live references unless they land under an excluded path such as souji-shokunin/tests/**.

Measured with ripgrep 15.2.0: the exclusion glob fires when the sweep runs with cwd = the fixture repo root and the search path `.` (canonical form) or when it is anchored as '!**/souji-shokunin/census/**'. It does NOT fire when rg is handed an absolute search root (`rg ... /abs/root -g '!souji-shokunin/census/**'`) or a relative root name other than `.`; a conforming tool must use one of the working forms, otherwise this case reports NOT-SAFE(stale-refs) and the D3 defect is still present.
mtime is set relative to run time (now - 3*86400 s), so the case stays deterministic on every run; --stale-days 1 is the default threshold used by the spec.
The target's content never contains its own basename; the only live mention in the whole fixture repo is the excluded decoy.
